best_for: Home users and small-office admins who already pay for cloud storage or own a NAS and want encrypted, scheduled backups of a few PCs without a backup subscription.

points.title: Encrypted before it leaves
points.text: Files are encrypted with AES-256 on your own machine before upload, so the storage provider only ever holds scrambled data. After the first run, only changed blocks are sent, which keeps later backups small and quick.

points.title: Use the storage you already have
points.text: Targets include Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Azure, Google Cloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, SFTP, FTP, WebDAV, SMB shares, a NAS or an external drive. You pay your storage provider, not Duplicati.

points.title: No account needed
points.text: The app itself is free and open source under the MIT license. On first start it asks whether to connect to the Duplicati Console, and you can skip that and back up locally. The settings live in a web page that opens in your browser.

points.title: The console is the paid part
points.text: The hosted console is free for up to 2 monitored machines and the last 200 backups. Pro adds missed-backup alerts and remote management for about USD 2 to 2.50 per machine per month, up to 100 machines. Enterprise starts at USD 3 per machine per month with a 10-machine minimum. points.title: Linux and NAS builds exist elsewhere
points.text: The project also ships .deb, .rpm, AppImage and Synology packages, including Arm7 builds for older Raspberry Pi boards. This site lists only Windows and Mac.

points.title: Installer details
points.text: The Windows MSI comes in x64, Arm64 and 32-bit x86 builds and installs for all users; the listing keeps 13 versions. The Mac build needs macOS 12 or later, for Intel and Apple silicon, and only the current release is listed. Installing a new version over the old one keeps your backup jobs.
